profile.name: Daniil Tenishev
profile.description: Daniel (kewldan), 18, ITMO Software Engineering. I build from the kernel up to the UI: XDP filters, Go backends, desktop apps and Telegram Mini Apps.

hero.headline: I build from the ==kernel== up to the _UI._
hero.lead: I build things from the kernel up to the UI: XDP filters, Go backends, desktop apps and Telegram Mini Apps. In production, used by real people.

about.pull: I'm Daniel, Daniil Tenishev on paper. 18, first year of Software Engineering at ITMO, group M3105, class of 2030. I live in Pushkin and ride into Saint Petersburg every day.
now: Working as a developer alongside uni
Building Omniflow, my own VPN service
about.traitsNote: Friends say that about me. I always want to know how things work inside. That is how I end up writing engines, protocols and a passport-chip reader. My strongest skill is solving problems.
about.hobbies: Travelling and games: 90 on Steam, mostly the kind where you build factories. If I weren't a programmer, I'd be a pilot.
about.desk: MacBook Pro M4 Pro. _best buy ever!_

work.title: Six projects.
work.lead: Each one gets its own stage. Jump straight to one, or scroll through all six.

projects.name: LarpGuard
projects.title: Cloudflare.
projects.lead: A bot filter in front of Traefik that reads **every layer** of a connection and asks one question: does this stack match the browser it claims to be?

specs.label: layers fingerprinted: TCP, TLS, HTTP/2, QUIC
proxy lists. RTT does the work.

points: TCP SYN, JA4/JA4T/JA4H, HTTP/2 and QUIC fingerprints scored into human, suspicious, bot and verified_bot
Proxy detection from the RTT gap between TCP and the TLS 1.3 handshake, without proxy lists
XDP/eBPF prefilter with its own loader; gradient-boosting inference in C++ in microseconds

projects.name: Omniflow
projects.title: A whole VPN business.
projects.lead: My own VPN business, turned into an open product: Telegram bot, subscriptions, payments, support, marketing and an admin panel on top of Remnawave, without owning Xray.

specs.label: payment providers: Telegram Stars, CryptoBot, YooKassa
admin roles with an audit log
ways to sign in: Argon2id, passkeys, TOTP, OIDC
1.26 with chi, pgx, sqlc and River

points: Plans, renewals and upgrades via Telegram Stars, CryptoBot or YooKassa; promo codes, wallet, referrals, tickets
RBAC admin: Argon2id, passkeys, TOTP, OIDC, 6 roles, audit log
Immutable plan versions, refunds, a wallet ledger, durable fulfilment through a transactional outbox

projects.name: Tether
projects.title: adb.
projects.lead: Every Android developer keeps a text file of adb commands. Tether puts all of it in one quiet, keyboard-first window.

back.alt: Tether: device overview with battery, storage, memory and CPU

specs.label: core on Tauri, talks the adb protocol

points: Screen mirroring with audio and recording, a file manager, APK installs to many devices at once
Logcat with crash detection, multi-tab shell, Wi-Fi pairing by QR, performance graphs
Talks to the adb server over its protocol instead of parsing the CLI; ⌘K palette, signed OTA updates

commits.message: feat: ship LarpGuard, Omniflow, Tether, m3105.ru
commits.body: Plus the ITMO C++ Lab Kit, and client work for ИСК «ВИТА» and ЖК «Экспоград».
GradesTracker and more Telegram projects, between exam prep.
The peak year: the OGE and a bot for its results, Mini Apps (Dnevnik, Sudooky), the first npm and PyPI packages, the first paid orders.
An OpenGL framework, VulkanEngine, MinecraftServerCore, the Logical System remaster, Lua for CC: Tweaked, and the first Telegram bots.
ConsolePong, ShooterGame on OpenGL, utilities for Project Zomboid.
My profile said “Java programmer from Russia” back then.
First real projects: a life simulation in Python.
Joined GitHub in July 2018. I was about ten.
